sections.label: First Adhyaya
sections.name: The Self sends forth the worlds and the Person
intro: The Aitareya belongs to the Rig Veda, where it forms part of the Aitareya Aranyaka. In the beginning, it says, there was only the Self, which sent forth the worlds, the cosmic Person and the powers of the senses, and then entered the body through the crown of the head to dwell in it. It ends in one of the four great sayings of the Vedanta: 'Consciousness is Brahman' (prajnanam brahma).
Adoration to the Highest Self Harih, Om!

verses.sa: आत्मा वा इदमेक एवाग्र आसीन्नान्यत्किञ्चन मिषत् ॥
verses.tr: ātmā vā idameka evāgra āsīnnānyatkiñcana miṣat
verses.en: Verily, in the beginning all this was Self, one only; there was nothing else blinking whatsoever.
verses.head: First Khanda

verses.sa:
स ईक्षत लोकान्नु सृजा इति ॥
स इमाँल्लोकानसृजत ॥
verses.tr:
sa īkṣata lokānnu sṛjā iti
sa imām̐llokānasṛjata
verses.en: He thought: 'Shall I send forth worlds?' He sent forth these worlds,

verses.sa: अम्भो मरीचीर्मरमापो ॥
verses.tr: ambho marīcīrmaramāpo
verses.en: Ambhas (water), Marichi (light), Mara (mortal), and Ap (water).

verses.sa:
अदोऽम्भः परेण दिवं द्यौः प्रतिष्ठाऽन्तरिक्षं मरीचयः ।
पृथिवी मरो या अधस्तात्त आपः ॥
verses.tr:
ado'mbhaḥ pareṇa divaṃ dyauḥ pratiṣṭhā'ntarikṣaṃ marīcayaḥ
pṛthivī maro yā adhastātta āpaḥ
verses.en: That Ambhas (water) is above the heaven, and it is heaven, the support. The Marichis (the lights) are the sky. The Mara (mortal) is the earth, and the waters under the earth are the Ap world.

verses.sa:
स ईक्षतेमे नु लोका लोकपालान्नु सृजा इति ॥
सोऽद्भ्य एव पुरुषं समुद्धृत्यामूर्छयत् ॥
verses.tr:
sa īkṣateme nu lokā lokapālānnu sṛjā iti
so'dbhya eva puruṣaṃ samuddhṛtyāmūrchayat
verses.en: He thought: 'There are these worlds; shall I send forth guardians of the worlds?' He then formed the Purusha (the person), taking him forth from the water.

verses.sa:
तमभ्यतपत्तस्याभितप्तस्य मुखं निरभिद्यत यथाऽण्डं मुखाद्वाग्वाचोऽग्निर्नासिके निरभिद्येतां नासिकाभ्यां प्राणः ।
प्राणाद्वायुरक्षिणी निरभिद्येतामक्षिभ्यां चक्षुश्चक्षुष आदित्यः कर्णौ निरभिद्येतां कर्णाभ्यां श्रोत्रं श्रोत्राद्दिशस्त्वङ्निरभिद्यत त्वचो लोमानि लोमभ्य ओषधिवनस्पतयो हृदयं निरभिद्यत हृदयान्मनो मनसश्चन्द्रमा नाभिर्निरभिद्यत नाभ्या अपानोऽपानान्मृत्युः शिश्नं निरभिद्यत शिश्नाद्रेतो रेतस आपः ॥
verses.tr:
tamabhyatapattasyābhitaptasya mukhaṃ nirabhidyata yathā'ṇḍaṃ mukhādvāgvāco'gnirnāsike nirabhidyetāṃ nāsikābhyāṃ prāṇaḥ
prāṇādvāyurakṣiṇī nirabhidyetāmakṣibhyāṃ cakṣuścakṣuṣa ādityaḥ karṇau nirabhidyetāṃ karṇābhyāṃ śrotraṃ śrotrāddiśastvaṅnirabhidyata tvaco lomāni lomabhya oṣadhivanaspatayo hṛdayaṃ nirabhidyata hṛdayānmano manasaścandramā nābhirnirabhidyata nābhyā apāno'pānānmṛtyuḥ śiśnaṃ nirabhidyata śiśnādreto retasa āpaḥ
verses.en: He brooded on him, and when that person had thus been brooded on, a mouth burst forth like an egg. From the mouth proceeded speech, from speech Agni (fire),. Nostrils burst forth. From the nostrils proceeded scent (prana), from scent Vayu (air). Eyes burst forth. From the eyes proceeded sight, from sight Aditya (sun). Ears burst forth. From the ears proceeded hearing, from hearing the Dis (quarters of the world). Skin burst forth. From the skin proceeded hairs (sense of touch), from the hairs shrubs and trees. The heart burst forth. From the heart proceeded mind, from mind Kandramas (moon). The navel burst forth. From the navel proceeded the apana (the down-breathing), from apana death. The generative organ burst forth. From the organ proceeded seed, from seed water.

verses.sa:
ता एता देवताः सृष्टा अस्मिन्महत्यर्णवे प्रापतन् ।
तमशनापिपासाभ्यामन्ववार्जत् ॥
verses.tr:
tā etā devatāḥ sṛṣṭā asminmahatyarṇave prāpatan
tamaśanāpipāsābhyāmanvavārjat
verses.en: Those deities (devata), Agni and the rest, after they had been sent forth, fell into this great ocean. Then he (the Self) besieged him, (the person) with hunger and thirst.
verses.head: Second Khanda

verses.sa:
ता एनमब्रुवन्नायतनं नः प्रजानीहि यस्मिन्प्रतिष्ठिता अन्नमदामेति ॥
ताभ्यो गामानयत्ता अब्रुवन्न वै नोऽयमलमिति ।
ताभ्योऽश्वमानयत्ता अब्रुवन्न वै नोऽयमलमिति ॥
ताभ्यः पुरुषमानयत्ता अब्रुवन् सुकृतं बतेति पुरुषो वाव सुकृतम् ॥
verses.tr:
tā enamabruvannāyatanaṃ naḥ prajānīhi yasminpratiṣṭhitā annamadāmeti
tābhyo gāmānayattā abruvanna vai no'yamalamiti
tābhyo'śvamānayattā abruvanna vai no'yamalamiti
tābhyaḥ puruṣamānayattā abruvan sukṛtaṃ bateti puruṣo vāva sukṛtam
verses.en: The deities then (tormented by hunger and thirst) spoke to him (the Self): 'Allow us a place in which we may rest and eat food' He led a cow towards them (the deities). They said: 'This is not enough.' He led a horse towards them. They said: 'This is not enough.' He led man towards them. Then they said: 'Well done, indeed.' Therefore man is well done.

verses.sa: ता अब्रवीद्यथायतनं प्रविशतेति ॥
verses.tr: tā abravīdyathāyatanaṃ praviśateti
verses.en: He said to them: 'Enter, each according to his place.'

verses.sa: अग्निर्वाग्भूत्वा मुखं प्राविशद्वायुः प्राणो भूत्वा नासिके प्राविशदादित्यश्चक्षुर्भूत्वाऽक्षिणी प्राविशद्दिशः श्रोत्रं भूत्वा कर्णौ प्राविशन्नोषधिवनस्पतयो लोमानि भूत्वा त्वचं प्राविशंश्चन्द्रमा मनो भूत्वा हृदयं प्राविशन्मृत्युरपानो भूत्वा नाभिं प्राविशदापो रेतो भूत्वा शिश्नं प्राविशन् ॥
verses.tr: agnirvāgbhūtvā mukhaṃ prāviśadvāyuḥ prāṇo bhūtvā nāsike prāviśadādityaścakṣurbhūtvā'kṣiṇī prāviśaddiśaḥ śrotraṃ bhūtvā karṇau prāviśannoṣadhivanaspatayo lomāni bhūtvā tvacaṃ prāviśaṃścandramā mano bhūtvā hṛdayaṃ prāviśanmṛtyurapāno bhūtvā nābhiṃ prāviśadāpo reto bhūtvā śiśnaṃ prāviśan
verses.en: Then Agni (fire), having become speech, entered the mouth. Vayu (air), having become scent, entered the nostrils. Aditya (sun), having become sight, entered the eyes. The Dis (regions), having become hearing, entered the ears. The shrubs and trees, having become hairs, entered the skin. Kandramas (the moon), having become mind, entered the heart. Death, having become down-breathing, entered the navel. The waters, having become seed, entered the generative organ.

verses.sa:
तमशनायापिपासे अब्रूतामावाभ्यामभिप्रजानीहीति ते अब्रवीदेतास्वेव वां देवतास्वाभजाम्येतासु भागिन्यौ करोमीति ।
तस्माद्यस्यै कस्यै च देवतायै हविर्गृह्यते भागिन्यावेवास्यामशनायापिपासे भवतः ॥
verses.tr:
tamaśanāyāpipāse abrūtāmāvābhyāmabhiprajānīhīti te abravīdetāsveva vāṃ devatāsvābhajāmyetāsu bhāginyau karomīti
tasmādyasyai kasyai ca devatāyai havirgṛhyate bhāginyāvevāsyāmaśanāyāpipāse bhavataḥ
verses.en: Then Hunger and Thirst spoke to him (the Self): 'Allow us two (a place).' He said to them: 'I assign you to those very deities there, I make you co-partners with them.' Therefore to whatever deity an oblation is offered, hunger and thirst are co-partners in it.

verses.sa:
स ईक्षतेमे नु लोकाश्च लोकपालाश्चान्नमेभ्यः सृजा इति ॥
सोऽपोऽभ्यतपत्ताभ्योऽभितप्ताभ्यो मूर्तिरजायत ।
या वै सा मूर्तिरजायतान्नं वै तत् ॥
verses.tr:
sa īkṣateme nu lokāśca lokapālāścānnamebhyaḥ sṛjā iti
so'po'bhyatapattābhyo'bhitaptābhyo mūrtirajāyata
yā vai sā mūrtirajāyatānnaṃ vai tat
verses.en: He thought: 'There are these worlds and the guardians of the worlds. Let me send forth food for them.' He brooded over the water. From the water thus brooded on, matter (murti) was born. And that matter which was born, that verily was food.
verses.head: Third Khanda

verses.sa:
तदेनत्सृष्टं पराङत्यजिघांसत्तद्वाचाऽजिघृक्षत् तन्नाशक्नोद्वाचा ग्रहीतुम् ।
स यद्धैनद्वाचाऽग्रहैष्यदभिव्याहृत्य हैवान्नमत्रप्स्यत् ॥
तत्प्राणेनाजिघृक्षत् तन्नाशक्नोत्प्राणेन ग्रहीतुम् ।
स यद्धैनत्प्राणेनाग्रहैष्यदभिप्राण्य हैवान्नमत्रप्स्यत् ॥
तच्चक्षुषाऽजिघृक्षत् तन्नाशक्नोच्चक्षुषा ग्रहीतुम् ।
स यद्धैनच्चक्षुषाऽग्रहैष्यद्दृष्ट्वा हैवान्नमत्रप्स्यत् ॥
तच्छ्रोत्रेणाजिघृक्षत् तन्नाशक्नोच्छ्रोत्रेण ग्रहीतुम् ।
स यद्धैनच्छ्रोत्रेणाग्रहैष्यच्छ्रुत्वा हैवान्नमत्रप्स्यत् ॥
तत्त्वचाऽजिघृक्षत् तन्नाशक्नोत्त्वचा ग्रहीतुम् ।
स यद्धैनत्त्वचाऽग्रहैष्यत् स्पृष्ट्वा हैवान्नमत्रप्स्यत् ॥
तन्मनसाऽजिघृक्षत् तन्नाशक्नोन्मनसा ग्रहीतुम् ।
स यद्धैनन्मनसाऽग्रहैष्यद्ध्यात्वा हैवान्नमत्रप्स्यत् ॥
तच्छिश्नेनाजिघृक्षत् तन्नाशक्नोच्छिश्नेन ग्रहीतुम् ।
स यद्धैनच्छिश्नेनाग्रहैष्यद्विसृज्य हैवान्नमत्रप्स्यत् ॥
तदपानेनाजिघृक्षत् तदावयत् ॥
verses.tr:
tadenatsṛṣṭaṃ parāṅatyajighāṃsattadvācā'jighṛkṣat tannāśaknodvācā grahītum
sa yaddhainadvācā'grahaiṣyadabhivyāhṛtya haivānnamatrapsyat
tatprāṇenājighṛkṣat tannāśaknotprāṇena grahītum
sa yaddhainatprāṇenāgrahaiṣyadabhiprāṇya haivānnamatrapsyat
taccakṣuṣā'jighṛkṣat tannāśaknoccakṣuṣā grahītum
sa yaddhainaccakṣuṣā'grahaiṣyaddṛṣṭvā haivānnamatrapsyat
tacchrotreṇājighṛkṣat tannāśaknocchrotreṇa grahītum
sa yaddhainacchrotreṇāgrahaiṣyacchrutvā haivānnamatrapsyat
tattvacā'jighṛkṣat tannāśaknottvacā grahītum
sa yaddhainattvacā'grahaiṣyat spṛṣṭvā haivānnamatrapsyat
tanmanasā'jighṛkṣat tannāśaknonmanasā grahītum
sa yaddhainanmanasā'grahaiṣyaddhyātvā haivānnamatrapsyat
tacchiśnenājighṛkṣat tannāśaknocchiśnena grahītum
sa yaddhainacchiśnenāgrahaiṣyadvisṛjya haivānnamatrapsyat
tadapānenājighṛkṣat tadāvayat
verses.en: When this food (the object matter) had thus been sent forth, it wished to flee, crying and turning away. He (the subject) tried to grasp it by speech. He could not grasp it by speech. If he had grasped it by speech, man would be satisfied by naming food. He tried to grasp it by scent (breath). He could not grasp it by scent. If he had grasped it by scent, man would be satisfied by smelling food. He tried to grasp it by the eye. He could not grasp it by the eye. If he had grasped it by the eye, man would be satisfied by seeing food. He tried to grasp it by the ear. He could not grasp it by the ear. If he had grasped it by the ear, man would be satisfied by hearing food. He tried to grasp it by the skin. He could not grasp it by the skin. If he had grasped it by the skin, man would be satisfied by touching food. He tried to grasp it by the mind. He could not grasp it by the mind. If he had grasped it by the mind, man would be satisfied by thinking food. He tried to grasp it by the generative organ. He could not grasp it by the organ. If he had grasped it by the organ, man would be satisfied by sending forth food. He tried to grasp it by the down-breathing (the breath which helps to swallow food through the mouth and to carry it off through the rectum, the payvindriya). He got it.

verses.sa: सैषोऽन्नस्य ग्रहो यद्वायुरनायुर्वा एष यद्वायुः ॥
verses.tr: saiṣo'nnasya graho yadvāyuranāyurvā eṣa yadvāyuḥ
verses.en: Thus it is Vayu (the getter) who lays hold of food, and the Vayu is verily Annayu (he who gives life or who lives by food).

verses.sa: स ईक्षत कथं न्विदं मदृते स्यादिति ॥
verses.tr: sa īkṣata kathaṃ nvidaṃ madṛte syāditi
verses.en: He thought: 'How can all this be without me?

verses.sa: स ईक्षत कतरेण प्रपद्या इति ॥
verses.tr: sa īkṣata katareṇa prapadyā iti
verses.en: And then he thought: By what way shall I get there?

verses.sa: स ईक्षत यदि वाचाऽभिव्याहृतं यदि प्राणेनाभिप्राणितं यदि चक्षुषा दृष्टं यदि श्रोत्रेण श्रुतं यदि त्वचा स्पृष्टं यदि मनसा ध्यातं यद्यपानेनाभ्यपानितं यदि शिश्नेन विसृष्टमथ कोऽहमिति ॥
verses.tr: sa īkṣata yadi vācā'bhivyāhṛtaṃ yadi prāṇenābhiprāṇitaṃ yadi cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭaṃ yadi śrotreṇa śrutaṃ yadi tvacā spṛṣṭaṃ yadi manasā dhyātaṃ yadyapānenābhyapānitaṃ yadi śiśnena visṛṣṭamatha ko'hamiti
verses.en: And then he thought: If speech names, if scent smells, if the eye sees, if the ear hears, if the skin feels, if the mind thinks, if the off-breathing digests, if the organ sends forth, then what am I?'

verses.sa: स एतमेव सीमानं विदर्यैतया द्वारा प्रापद्यत ॥
verses.tr: sa etameva sīmānaṃ vidaryaitayā dvārā prāpadyata
verses.en: Then opening the suture of the skull, he got in by that door.

verses.sa: सैषा विदृतिर्नाम द्वास्तदेतन्नान्दनम् ॥
verses.tr: saiṣā vidṛtirnāma dvāstadetannāndanam
verses.en: That door is called the Vidriti (tearing asunder), the Nandana (the place of bliss).

verses.sa: तस्य त्रय आवसथास्त्रयः स्वप्ना अयमावसथोऽयमावसथोऽयमावसथ इति ॥
verses.tr: tasya traya āvasathāstrayaḥ svapnā ayamāvasatho'yamāvasatho'yamāvasatha iti
verses.en: There are three dwelling-places for him, three dreams; this dwelling-place (the eye), this dwelling-place (the throat), this dwelling-place (the heart).

verses.sa:
स जातो भूतान्यभिव्यैख्यत् किमिहान्यं वावदिषदिति ।
स एतमेव पुरुषं ब्रह्म ततममपश्यत् ।
इदमदर्शमिती३ ॥
verses.tr:
sa jāto bhūtānyabhivyaikhyat kimihānyaṃ vāvadiṣaditi
sa etameva puruṣaṃ brahma tatamamapaśyat
idamadarśamitī3
verses.en: When born (when the Highest Self had entered the body) he looked through all things, in order to see whether anything wished to proclaim here another (Self). He saw this person only (himself) as the widely spread Brahman. 'I saw it,' thus he said; Therefore he was Idam-dra (seeing this).

verses.sa:
तस्मादिदन्द्रो नामेदन्द्रो ह वै नाम तमिदन्द्रं सन्तमिन्द्र इत्याचक्षते परोक्षेण ।
परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवाः परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवाः ॥
verses.tr:
tasmādidandro nāmedandro ha vai nāma tamidandraṃ santamindra ityācakṣate parokṣeṇa
parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ
verses.en: Being Idamdra by name, they call him Indra mysteriously. For the Devas love mystery, yea, they love mystery.

sections.label: Second Adhyaya
sections.name: The three births of the Self

verses.en: Let the women who are with child move away!

verses.sa: पुरुषे ह वा अयमादितो गर्भो भवति यदेतद्रेतः ॥
verses.tr: puruṣe ha vā ayamādito garbho bhavati yadetadretaḥ
verses.en: Verily, from the beginning he (the self) is in man as a germ, which is called seed.

verses.sa: तदेतत्सर्वेभ्योऽङ्गेभ्यस्तेजः सम्भूतमात्मन्येवात्मानं बिभर्ति तद्यदा स्त्रियां सिञ्चत्यथैनज्जनयति तदस्य प्रथमं जन्म ॥
verses.tr: tadetatsarvebhyo'ṅgebhyastejaḥ sambhūtamātmanyevātmānaṃ bibharti tadyadā striyāṃ siñcatyathainajjanayati tadasya prathamaṃ janma
verses.en: This (seed), which is strength gathered from all the limbs of the body, he (the man) bears as self in his self (body). When he commits the seed to the woman, then he (the father) causes it to be born. That is his first birth.

verses.sa:
तत्स्त्रिया आत्मभूयं गच्छति यथा स्वमङ्गं तथा ।
तस्मादेनां न हिनस्ति ॥
verses.tr:
tatstriyā ātmabhūyaṃ gacchati yathā svamaṅgaṃ tathā
tasmādenāṃ na hinasti
verses.en: That seed becomes the self of the woman, as if one of her own limbs. Therefore it does not injure her.

verses.sa:
साऽस्यैतमात्मानमत्र गतं भावयति ॥
सा भावयित्री भावयितव्या भवति ॥
verses.tr:
sā'syaitamātmānamatra gataṃ bhāvayati
sā bhāvayitrī bhāvayitavyā bhavati
verses.en: She nourishes his (her husband's) self (the son) within her. She who nourishes, is to be nourished.

verses.sa:
तं स्त्री गर्भं बिभर्ति ।
सोऽग्र एव कुमारं जन्मनोऽग्रेऽधिभावयति ॥
verses.tr:
taṃ strī garbhaṃ bibharti
so'gra eva kumāraṃ janmano'gre'dhibhāvayati
verses.en: The woman bears the germ. He (the father) elevates the child even before the birth, and immediately after.

verses.sa: स यत्कुमारं जन्मनोऽग्रेऽधिभावयत्यात्मानमेव तद्भावयत्येषां लोकानां सन्तत्या ॥
verses.tr: sa yatkumāraṃ janmano'gre'dhibhāvayatyātmānameva tadbhāvayatyeṣāṃ lokānāṃ santatyā
verses.en: When he thus elevates the child both before and after his birth, he really elevates his own self,

verses.sa: एवं सन्तता हीमे लोकाः ॥
verses.tr: evaṃ santatā hīme lokāḥ
verses.en: For the continuation of these worlds (men). For thus are these worlds continued.

verses.sa: तदस्य द्वितीयं जन्म ॥
verses.tr: tadasya dvitīyaṃ janma
verses.en: This is his second birth.

verses.sa: सोऽस्यायमात्मा पुण्येभ्यः कर्मभ्यः प्रतिधीयते ॥
verses.tr: so'syāyamātmā puṇyebhyaḥ karmabhyaḥ pratidhīyate
verses.en: He (the son), being his self, is then placed in his stead for (the performance of) all good works.

verses.sa: अथास्यायमितर आत्मा कृतकृत्यो वयोगतः प्रैति ॥
verses.tr: athāsyāyamitara ātmā kṛtakṛtyo vayogataḥ praiti
verses.en: But his other self (the father), having done all he has to do, and having reached the full measure of his life, departs.

verses.sa: स इतः प्रयन्नेव पुनर्जायते तदस्य तृतीयं जन्म ॥
verses.tr: sa itaḥ prayanneva punarjāyate tadasya tṛtīyaṃ janma
verses.en: And departing from hence he is born again. That is his third birth.

verses.sa: तदुक्तमृषिणा ॥
verses.tr: taduktamṛṣiṇā
verses.en: And this has been declared by a Rishi (Rv. IV, 27, 1):

verses.sa: गर्भे नु सन्नन्वेषामवेदमहं देवानां जनिमानि विश्वा शतं मा पुर आयसीररक्षन्नधः श्येनो जवसा निरदीयमिति ॥
verses.tr: garbhe nu sannanveṣāmavedamahaṃ devānāṃ janimāni viśvā śataṃ mā pura āyasīrarakṣannadhaḥ śyeno javasā niradīyamiti
verses.en: 'While dwelling in the womb, I discovered all the births of these Devas. A hundred iron strongholds kept me, but I escaped quickly down like a falcon.'

verses.sa:
गर्भ एवैतच्छयानो वामदेव एवमुवाच ॥
स एवं विद्वानस्माच्छरीरभेदादूर्ध्व उत्क्रम्यामुष्मिन् स्वर्गे लोके सर्वान् कामानाप्त्वाऽमृतः समभवत् समभवत् ॥
verses.tr:
garbha evaitacchayāno vāmadeva evamuvāca
sa evaṃ vidvānasmāccharīrabhedādūrdhva utkramyāmuṣmin svarge loke sarvān kāmānāptvā'mṛtaḥ samabhavat samabhavat
verses.en: Vamadeva, lying in the womb, has thus declared this. And having this knowledge he stepped forth, after this dissolution of the body, and having obtained all his desires in that heavenly world, became immortal, yea, he became immortal.
Let the women go back to their place.

verses.sa: कोऽयमात्मेति वयमुपास्महे कतरः स आत्मा ॥
verses.tr: ko'yamātmeti vayamupāsmahe kataraḥ sa ātmā
verses.en: Who is he whom we meditate on as the Self? Which is the Self?

verses.sa:
येन वा पश्यति येन वा शृणोति येन वा गन्धानाजिघ्रति येन वा वाचं व्याकरोति येन वा स्वादु चास्वादु च विजानाति ॥
यदेतद्धृदयं मनश्चैतत् ।
सञ्ज्ञानमाज्ञानं विज्ञानं प्रज्ञानं मेधा दृष्टिर्धृतिर्मतिर्मनीषा जूतिः स्मृतिः सङ्कल्पः क्रतुरसुः कामो वश इति ॥
verses.tr:
yena vā paśyati yena vā śṛṇoti yena vā gandhānājighrati yena vā vācaṃ vyākaroti yena vā svādu cāsvādu ca vijānāti
yadetaddhṛdayaṃ manaścaitat
sañjñānamājñānaṃ vijñānaṃ prajñānaṃ medhā dṛṣṭirdhṛtirmatirmanīṣā jūtiḥ smṛtiḥ saṅkalpaḥ kraturasuḥ kāmo vaśa iti
verses.en: That by which we see (form), that by which we hear (sound), that by which we perceive smells, that by which we utter speech, that by which we distinguish sweet and not sweet, and what comes from the heart and the mind, namely, perception, command, understanding, knowledge, wisdom, seeing, holding, thinking, considering, readiness (or suffering), remembering, conceiving, willing, breathing, loving, desiring?

verses.sa: सर्वाण्येवैतानि प्रज्ञानस्य नामधेयानि भवन्ति ॥
verses.tr: sarvāṇyevaitāni prajñānasya nāmadheyāni bhavanti
verses.en: No, all these are various names only of knowledge (the true Self).

verses.sa:
एष ब्रह्मैष इन्द्र एष प्रजापतिरेते सर्वे देवा इमानि च पञ्चमहाभूतानि पृथिवी वायुराकाश आपो ज्योतींषीत्येतानीमानि च क्षुद्रमिश्राणीव ।
बीजानीतराणि चेतराणि चाण्डजानि च जारुजानि च स्वेदजानि चोद्भिज्जानि चाश्वा गावः पुरुषा हस्तिनो यत्किञ्चेदं प्राणि जङ्गमं च पतत्रि च यच्च स्थावरं सर्वं तत्प्रज्ञानेत्रं ॥
verses.tr:
eṣa brahmaiṣa indra eṣa prajāpatirete sarve devā imāni ca pañcamahābhūtāni pṛthivī vāyurākāśa āpo jyotīṃṣītyetānīmāni ca kṣudramiśrāṇīva
bījānītarāṇi cetarāṇi cāṇḍajāni ca jārujāni ca svedajāni codbhijjāni cāśvā gāvaḥ puruṣā hastino yatkiñcedaṃ prāṇi jaṅgamaṃ ca patatri ca yacca sthāvaraṃ sarvaṃ tatprajñānetraṃ
verses.en: And that Self, consisting of (knowledge), is Brahman (m.), it is Indra, it is Prajapati. All these Devas, these five great elements, earth, air, ether, water, fire, these and those which are, as it were, small and mixed, and seeds of this kind and that kind, born from eggs, born from the womb, born from heat, born from germs, horses, cows, men, elephants, and whatsoever breathes, whether walking or flying, and what is immoveable-all that is led (produced) by knowledge (the Self).

verses.sa: प्रज्ञाने प्रतिष्ठितं प्रज्ञानेत्रो लोकः प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठा ॥
verses.tr: prajñāne pratiṣṭhitaṃ prajñānetro lokaḥ prajñā pratiṣṭhā
verses.en: It rests on knowledge (the Self). The world is led (produced) by knowledge (the Self). Knowledge is its cause.

verses.sa: प्रज्ञानं ब्रह्म ॥
verses.tr: prajñānaṃ brahma
verses.en: Knowledge is Brahman.

verses.sa: स एतेन प्राज्ञेनाऽऽत्मनाऽस्माल्लोकादुत्क्रम्यामुष्मिन्स्वर्गे लोके सर्वान् कामानाप्त्वाऽमृतः समभवत् समभवत् ॥
verses.tr: sa etena prājñenā''tmanā'smāllokādutkramyāmuṣminsvarge loke sarvān kāmānāptvā'mṛtaḥ samabhavat samabhavat
verses.en: He (Vamadeva), having by this conscious self stepped forth from this world, and having obtained all desires in that heavenly world, became immortal, yea, he became immortal. Thus it is, Om.

verses.sa:
वाङ् मे मनसि प्रतिष्ठिता मनो मे वाचि प्रतिष्ठितमाविरावीर्म एधि ॥
वेदस्य म आणीस्थः श्रुतं मे मा प्रहासीरनेनाधीतेनाहोरात्रान् सन्दधाम्यृतं वदिष्यामि सत्यं वदिष्यामि ॥
तन्मामवतु तद्वक्तारमवत्ववतु मामवतु वक्तारमवतु वक्तारम् ॥
ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः ॥
verses.tr:
vāṅ me manasi pratiṣṭhitā mano me vāci pratiṣṭhitamāvirāvīrma edhi
vedasya ma āṇīsthaḥ śrutaṃ me mā prahāsīranenādhītenāhorātrān sandadhāmyṛtaṃ vadiṣyāmi satyaṃ vadiṣyāmi
tanmāmavatu tadvaktāramavatvavatu māmavatu vaktāramavatu vaktāram
oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ
verses.en: My speech rests in the mind, my mind rests in speech. Appear to me (thou, the Highest Self)! You (speech and mind) are the two pins (that hold the wheels) of the Veda. May what I have learnt not forsake me. I join day and night with what I have learnt. I shall speak of the real, I shall speak the true. May this protect me, may this protect the teacher! May it protect me, may it protect the teacher, yea, the teacher!
